text: Given a known Global Administrator's user_id in a connected Microsoft Graph tenant, When graph_list_user_roles(user_id) is called, Then the response's roles list includes an entry with display_name "Global Administrator" and classification "active"

Given a known Global Administrator's user_id in a customer tenant reached via GDAP, When graph_list_user_roles(customer_tenant_id, user_id) is called, Then the response's roles list includes an entry with display_name "Global Administrator"

Given graph_list_user_roles returns a non-empty roles list, When a returned entry is inspected, Then it carries display_name, classification, and scope (classification is "active" and scope is "directory" for every entry in this slice)

Given the ms-graph-mcp server's tool list, When graph_list_user_roles is inspected, Then it is registered with exactly one required parameter, user_id, and no customer_tenant_id (single-tenant connector)

Given the gdap-mcp server's tool list, When graph_list_user_roles is inspected, Then it is registered with customer_tenant_id as a required parameter in addition to user_id (mirrors every other ported Graph tool, e.g. graph_get_user)

Given a full test run exercising graph_list_user_roles in both connectors (TC1/TC2/TC7/TC8), When the fake Microsoft Graph server's call log is inspected afterwards, Then it recorded zero PATCH/POST/DELETE requests attributable to this tool -- only GET
Given a user_id with no directory role assignment, When graph_list_user_roles(user_id) is called, Then the response is {user_id, count: 0, roles: []}, not an error

Given a user_id that does not exist in the tenant, When graph_list_user_roles(user_id) is called, Then the response is the same structured 404 error envelope every other user-scoped tool returns (error/message/retryable), not an unhandled exception
